market_question: US x Iran permanent peace deal by June 30, 2026?
reasoning: A permanent peace deal between the US and Iran by mid-2026 is highly implausible given decades of frozen relations, domestic hardliner constraints in both countries, and the lack of any framework for lasting coexistence. Even if temporary ceasefires occur, a definitive end to military hostilities within this short timeframe is far-fetched. The market’s 25.5% implied probability is a drastic overestimate.
evidence_points: The US and Iran have no formal diplomatic ties and have been in a state of de facto hostility since 1980.
Any US administration would face fierce Congressional and allied opposition to a permanent peace deal without major Iranian concessions, which are unlikely.
Iran’s political system is built in part on anti-American ideology; a permanent peace would require a revolutionary shift, improbable by mid-2026.
Even the JCPOA (2015) was a limited nuclear deal and did not permanently end military hostilities; it later collapsed.
The market’s own description references a ‘two-week ceasefire’ in April 2026, suggesting even that would be temporary, not permanent.
sources_consulted: General knowledge of US-Iran relations, historical diplomatic context, structure of Iranian regime
